title: Weight-Based Dosing
definition: Every pediatric drug dose is calculated from the child's weight in kilograms, then double-checked by two nurses. A decimal slip can mean a tenfold overdose, so independent verification is mandatory. The Broselow tape gives emergency doses by length when there is no time to weigh.
equipment: Broselow tapes and pediatric crash carts
patient_flow: Children arrive via the ED, clinic referral, or scheduled admission, and are placed on units grouped by age when possible. Parents room in, rounds include the family, and every medication is double-checked by weight. Discharge teaching covers home care, warning signs, and follow-up, with school notes when needed.
code_demo:
def pediatric_dose(weight_kg, mg_per_kg, max_dose=None):
    """Weight-based pediatric dose calculator with safety cap."""
    dose = weight_kg * mg_per_kg
    if max_dose and dose > max_dose:
        return f"{max_dose} mg (capped at max)"
    return f"{round(dose,1)} mg for {weight_kg} kg child"
print(pediatric_dose(18, 15, max_dose=1000))  # amoxicillin example
teaching: Simple: the core idea in plain words — what it is and why it matters.
